title: AWS Trainium: The Journey for Designing and Optimization Full Stack ML Hardware
problem: Machine learning accelerators require coordinated design decisions across chip architecture, instruction sets, server design, compilers, and both inter- and intra-chip connectivity, creating complex interdependencies that siloed design approaches cannot effectively resolve.
motivation: Holistic full-stack optimization from silicon to software is critical for achieving both high performance and ease of use in ML systems, requiring deep integration across traditionally separate design domains.
method: AWS built the entire system as one unit—chip, servers, network infrastructure, compilers (software that translates code for hardware), and runtime software (what executes that code). Because one organization owned all these layers, designers could make changes and immediately coordinate across teams rather than each group working in isolation. They prioritized simplicity and usability over maximum performance in any single component. Through three product generations, they made design tradeoffs with full-system context—accepting a cost in one layer if it meant better efficiency across the whole system.
key_novelty: AWS unified ownership of all system layers—chip, servers, networks, compilers (code translation software), and runtime—enabling each design decision to account for full-system impacts rather than optimizing each part independently.
contributions: Design principles and methodology for full-stack ML hardware development across chip to compiler layers
Evolution and improvements demonstrated across three generations of AWS Trainium products
Design tradeoffs and lessons learned from collaborative full-stack optimization approach
Framework integrating compiler optimization, runtime tools, and hardware architecture design
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; paper focuses on design journey and principles rather than experimental performance evaluation.
primary_theme: Full-stack ML hardware co-design and optimization
